senses.definition: A container made of rigid material, often with a handle, used to carry liquids or small items.
examples: I need a bucket to carry the water from the well.

quotes.text: The crab was cool and very light. But the water was thick with sand, and so, scrambling down, Jacob was about to jump, holding his bucket in front of him, when he saw, stretched entirely rigid, side by side, their faces very red, an enormous man and woman.
quotes.reference: 1922, Virginia Woolf, chapter 1, in Jacob's Room:

senses.definition: The amount held in this container.
examples: The horse drank a whole bucket of water.

senses.definition: (informal, chiefly in the plural) A large amount of liquid.
examples: I was so nervous that I sweated buckets.

senses.definition: (informal, chiefly in the plural) A great deal of anything.
examples: My new suit cost me buckets.

senses.definition: (UK, archaic) A unit of measure equal to four gallons.
Part of a piece of machinery that resembles a bucket (container).
(MTE, slang, derogatory) Someone who habitually uses crack cocaine.
(slang) An old vehicle that is not in good working order.
(basketball, informal) The basket.
examples: The forward drove to the bucket.

senses.definition: (basketball, informal) A field goal.
examples: We can't keep giving up easy buckets.
